content.comment_body: Hello experts, is it possible to use this password BBHÿ@bb for [product_name]? Also, how can Unicode be used in a password?

Greetings [user_name], which version of [product_name] module do you have? As mentioned in the manual, it's best to use uppercase letters with a maximum length of ten characters. You might want to check the section 'Assigning a program password from the [product_name] Basic' on page 92 of the current manual: [url] Hope this helps.
Hi [user_name], referring to the manual: Passwords can only be up to 10 characters long and should consist of uppercase letters.
Hello experts, I really do have this password, but I'm unsure how to enter the two characters ÿ@ into [product_name]. When I try, I get an alert that only A-Z is allowed. Thank you in advance.
Hello, passwords must be entered using the same method as on the [product_name] device. You can't use unusual characters, just uppercase A-Z.

Hello, I am trying to upload a [product_name] program but I do not have the password, so I retrieved this password (BBHÿ@) from the program using a port monitor tool. Is it possible to use this password?
Hi, passwords are usually kept secret. How did you obtain this one? If you've downloaded it from the program, there might be no password set. Are you sure this password is for [product_name]?

Hi, as others have mentioned, passwords should only include capital letters. With the latest firmware change for [version_no], the monitor program may not show the correct password. You can delete the user program and password, then download a new one. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are seeking clarification on password requirements for [product_name], specifically with the use of special or Unicode characters. The system restricts passwords to uppercase letters only, which does not match user expectations and results in error messages. Documentation does explain these rules, but users would benefit from clearer and more explicit guidance on acceptable password formats.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to enter passwords containing special and Unicode characters and are looking for clear information on which formats are supported for [product_name] devices.
